method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across remembrance and presence, letters and the wish for news, delayed replies and interrupted routes, nearness across distance through a shared spiritual center, mirrors, light and the language of the heart, portraits of remembrance, gatherings that include the absent, prayer and the departed with their qualifications, and the fruits of connection in service and speech. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: spiritual association does not depend upon physical contact
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to departing pilgrims that spiritual association does not depend upon physical contact; a concise principle at a moment of parting.

selected.text: that establishes communication between the hearts of men. It is Love that confers eternal life. It is Love that bestows unfailing joy. If real Love appears in the heart of man, he will attract all the virtues. Love is the divine power which causes
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that Love establishes communication between hearts, confers eternal life and attracts all virtues; the source of the fruits.

selected.text: Watchfulness, association, gentleness and love are essential.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá naming watchfulness, association, gentleness and love as essential; practical virtues of connection.

selected.text: As ye laboured, 'Abdu'l-Baha too was with you in spirit, heart and soul.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá telling workers that as they laboured He was with them in spirit, heart and soul; presence in service.

selected.text: If you are attracted by spiritual fragrances, I will always be with you.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promising that if the hearer is attracted by spiritual fragrances He will always be with them; names the condition of presence.

selected.text: for the hearts of the friends of Baha are mirrors reflecting the Abha Kingdom
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling the hearts of the friends mirrors reflecting the Abha Kingdom; a brief statement of the mirror image.

selected.text: By My life! We have found the fragrance of My love in every word of thy letter
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh declaring that He found the fragrance of His love in every word of a letter; a brief and intimate image of fragrance in writing.

selected.text: My thoughts are turned towards you, and my heart leaps within me at your mention.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: This is a remembrance from Us to him who hath believed in the One, the All-Knowing
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh calling itself a remembrance from Him to one who has believed; the Tablet as divine remembrance.

selected.text: though I am physically absent, in truth I am present among them in spirit and heart
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that though physically absent He is present among the friends in spirit and heart; a concise assurance to a gathering.

selected.text: I am now viewing the flowers in the little garden and remembering thy rose-like face.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá viewing flowers in a little garden and remembering a friend’s rose-like face; a tender narrative moment.

selected.text: Yes, but they do not do it through medums nor in material ways, but in spiritual ways.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá answering that the departed communicate not through mediums nor in material ways but spiritually; the key qualification on mediums.

selected.text: you must at every moment convey a message from the most exalted realm to the lower world
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying the recipient must at every moment convey a message from the most exalted realm to the lower world; the believer as a living message.

selected.text: the holy spirits of those two pure souls may become joyous and glad in the luminous world
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping the holy spirits of two pure souls may become joyous and glad in the luminous world; the living gladdening the departed.

selected.text: like one absent yet present, conversed with you and made mention of some spiritual matters
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing conversing with a correspondent like one absent yet present; a compact statement of the absent-present paradox.

selected.text: When one perceives the fragrance of love from another, ultimate joy and delight is attained
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that perceiving the fragrance of love from another brings ultimate joy; a brief statement of mutual delight.

selected.text: If I cannot see each one of you individually every day that should not undermine our real love.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that not seeing each person every day should not undermine real love; applies the principle within a local community.

selected.text: Unclose thy spiritual ear that thou mayest become intimate with the call of the celestial Herald.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding the reader unclose the spiritual ear to become intimate with the celestial Herald; a practical call to listening.

selected.text: spiritual relations should also be established, for the foundation of these relations is spiritual
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that spiritual relations should be established, since the foundation of all relations is spiritual; a brief principle.

selected.text: I wished to also express my longing to meet with you, though I left this to the heart's attractions.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá leaving the expression of His longing to meet to the heart’s attractions; a delicate example of unspoken longing.

selected.text: The face speaks with face, the eyes with eyes, the hearts with hearts, and the spirits with spirits.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that face speaks with face, eyes with eyes, hearts with hearts and spirits with spirits; a memorable progression.

selected.text: But it was possible to communicate with the dead through the condition of the character and the heart.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that communication with the dead is possible through the condition of character and heart; the inward condition of communion.

selected.text: Through divine bounties, without need for paper and pen, our spiritual communion will be everlasting
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that through divine bounties, without paper and pen, spiritual communion will be everlasting; a concise promise.

selected.text: though physically distant, are spiritually near; though far to outward sight, are close in inner vision
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing friends who, though physically distant and far to outward sight, are near in inner vision; a compact statement of spiritual nearness.

selected.text: When two hearts are united together astonishing results will be seen. But a perfect union is necessary.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that when two hearts are united astonishing results appear, but perfect union is needed; opens the section on fruits.

selected.text: correspondence, in the estimation of them that have recognized the truth, is the perfection of communion
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh calling correspondence, in the estimation of those who have recognized the truth, the perfection of communion; a concise foundational statement on letters.

selected.text: Although this servant was not physically present in that gathering, in spirit I was intimate and present.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that though not physically present in a gathering, in spirit He was intimate and present; a concise assurance.

selected.text: Though I do not converse with you through the tongue, I commune with you through heart and soul and life.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that though He does not converse through the tongue He communes through heart, soul and life; inward speech in person.

selected.text: The Spirit knoweth the spirit, the Spirit addresseth the spirit and the Spirit associateth with the spirit.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá declaring that the Spirit knoweth, addresseth and associateth with the spirit; a terse foundational formula.

selected.text: At that time we will draw unto each other in spirit, a nearness which will be eternal, everlasting and endless.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promising a nearness in spirit that will be eternal, everlasting and endless; the promise of future nearness.

selected.text: In the Kingdom of holiness they chant the verses of the supreme gift and encourage you to follow their example
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that in the Kingdom of holiness they chant the verses of the supreme gift and encourage the living to follow their example; souls in the Kingdom as exemplars.

selected.text: Consider what a bounty the Lord of creation hath bestowed, that hearts have become thus connected to one another.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá inviting reflection on the bounty that hearts have become thus connected to one another; gratitude for the bond.

selected.text: I shall never forget thee. I remember thee always and desire for thee heavenly illumination and Baha'i spirituality.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promising never to forget the recipient and desiring heavenly illumination for them; remembrance joined to prayer.

selected.text: when hearts face each other and thought and contemplation take hold, connection and unity and harmony become realized
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that when hearts face each other in contemplation, connection and unity are realized; names the condition of harmony.

selected.text: For four years communication between us was cut off, but with heart and soul the spiritual messenger was continuous.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that through four years of severed communication the spiritual messenger was continuous; a concrete instance of long separation.

selected.text: Not a moment passes but that you come to mind, and not a breath is drawn but that your mention becomes our companion.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying not a breath is drawn but the recipient’s mention becomes His companion; a brief image of companionship in memory.

selected.text: The portals of the Kingdom are wide open and the inner ears are continually attuned to the Voice of the Lord of Hosts
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying the portals of the Kingdom are open and inner ears attuned to the Voice of the Lord; receptivity to the divine voice.

selected.text: I beseech God that thou mayest make Kurdistan a rose-garden and illuminate that land with the light of the love of God
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá beseeching that the recipient make Kurdistan a rose-garden with the light of the love of God; the bond issuing in service.

selected.text: But the good souls are given eternal life, and sometimes God permits their thoughts to reach the earth to help people.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that God sometimes permits the thoughts of good souls to reach the earth to help people; inspiration from the departed.

selected.text: Though we are distant in the world of dust, yet by virtue of the pure realm we are near, gathered in a single assembly.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that though distant in the world of dust they are gathered in a single assembly by virtue of the pure realm; the single assembly.

selected.text: You should speak about spiritual and godly things, in order that your souls may be revived and your minds be made pure.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to students that they should speak of spiritual things so that souls are revived and minds made pure; speech that helps.

selected.text: There is no mightier bond in the world of being than the attachment of the heart. Even a chain of steel hath not
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: When the friends are remembered, the heart and soul become adorned with the flowers and fragrances of hoped-for bounties.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that remembrance of the friends adorns heart and soul with flowers and fragrances; the fruit of remembering.

selected.text: and become intimate with the denizens of the Supreme Concourse, that thou mayest receive fresh inspiration in every moment
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá urging intimacy with the denizens of the Supreme Concourse to receive fresh inspiration every moment; links communion with inspiration.

selected.text: Thy letter contained most cheering good news and indicated the oneness of spiritual state that exists amongst the believers
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá finding in a letter cheering news of the oneness of spiritual state among the believers; links correspondence to unity.

selected.text: to the intense connection that exists between hearts, we are day and night eagerly awaiting news and hoping to receive word. We beseech God to grant such confirmations that from
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying the intense connection between hearts makes Him eagerly await news day and night; longing for news within inward connection.

selected.text: And with pure hearts, 'Abdu'l-Baha has complete and sufficient communion with the friends from heart and soul at every moment.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying He has complete communion with pure-hearted friends at every moment; closes the images with purity of heart.

selected.text: Physical meeting has no importance. The meeting is spiritual. Therefore, they should not be unhappy. They should be rejoiced
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that physical meeting has no importance, the meeting being spiritual, so those absent should rejoice; consolation for those who cannot come.

selected.text: Though the distance is great and the boundless ocean lies between us, you are companions and confidants, friends and intimates
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that though a boundless ocean lies between, the recipients are companions and confidants; friendship across the sea.

selected.text: But I swear by the Most Great Name that in the world of spirit and heart I am and have always been engaged in remembering you
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá swearing by the Most Great Name that in the world of spirit He has always been engaged in remembering the recipient; remembrance as oath.

selected.text:
The Blessed Leaves, particularly Her Highness, the Greatest Holy Leaf,
constantly make mention of thee and remember thee fondly
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá telling that the Blessed Leaves, particularly the Greatest Holy Leaf, constantly make fond mention of the recipient; a named portrait of remembrance.

selected.text: The nearness and remoteness of the physical world has no importance, for true affection and connection is of the heart and soul.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying physical nearness and remoteness have no importance since true affection is of heart and soul; a plain principle.

selected.text: The traces of the Pen of love and purity have bestowed purity upon the world and removed the dust of events from hearts and souls.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh saying the traces of the Pen of love and purity have removed the dust of events from hearts and souls; writing as purification.

selected.text: when I circumambulate around the point of attraction of the hearts of the denizens of the Kingdom, I immediately call thee to mind
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that when circumambulating the Shrine He immediately calls the recipient to mind; remembrance at the holy place.

selected.text: A letter arrived from Furugh and when opened it had a radiance and light. The words were like glass and the meanings like a lamp.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing a letter whose words were like glass and meanings like a lamp; a memorable image of a letter’s radiance.

selected.text: They were most pleased and happy with thee. In such a gathering they engaged in thy remembrance and became intimate with thy memory.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing others who, pleased with the recipient, engaged in their remembrance in a gathering; remembrance by the community.

selected.text: Although outwardly we are separated, in reality we are always intimately connected in heart and spirit and ever present and watchful
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that though outwardly separated they are always connected in heart and spirit and ever watchful; mutual watchfulness.

selected.text: Correspondence and communication are the two greatest means for solidarity. It is said that Correspondence is equal to half-meeting.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá naming correspondence and communication the two greatest means for solidarity; ties letters to unity.

selected.text: This is like two mirrors opposite each other; and from the other, back to the first; for it is the one sun which shines in them both.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on two facing mirrors lit by the one sun; grounds the mirror image in a common source.

selected.text: Night and day we are not free from mentioning those spiritual beloved ones and divine friends, and we beseech confirmation and success.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that night and day He mentions the spiritual beloved ones and beseeches confirmation for them; remembrance as prayer.

selected.text: Although I cannot converse with you in detail, my heart and spirit converse with you and share secrets without the tongue of utterance.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that though unable to converse in detail His heart and spirit share secrets without the tongue; inward speech in person.

selected.text: When this connection exists, bodily separation is not important; this condition is beyond the world of words and above all description.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that where this connection exists bodily separation is unimportant and beyond all description; marks the limit of words.

selected.text: In truth, letters have been and are half of meeting and encounter. In any case, they are the cause of gladness and the source of joy
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh calling letters half of meeting and encounter and a source of joy; the proverbial measure of what a letter achieves.

selected.text: this servant has taken up the pen so that a drop from the oceans of love surging in the heart might flow through the channel of the pen
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh taking up the pen so that a drop from the oceans of love in the heart may flow through it; a vivid image of writing as love’s overflow.

selected.text: such a connection, harmony and union has been achieved that on such a night, I am intimately engaged in remembrance of that kind friend
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying such connection has been achieved that on a given night He is engaged in remembrance of a kind friend; a particular moment.

selected.text: Although up to this time I have not written thee yet spiritual communication united the hearts and ideal correspondence was uninterrupted.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that before He had written, spiritual communication already united the hearts; communion preceding correspondence.

selected.text: Although material communication is cut off and no proper and sufficient correspondence can be maintained, you are nevertheless in my heart.
selected.reason: Words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá conveyed in a letter, saying that though material communication is cut off the recipient remains in His heart; continuity across interruption.

selected.text: O thou who gazest upon the face that is turned toward the Kingdom of Abha and the hidden and invisible Dominion! Commune in prayer and say:
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding one who gazes toward the Kingdom to commune in prayer; carries the addresses through to prayer.

selected.text: Though the mirror and the lights have no physical connection, yet the relationship of rays and reflected effulgences is firm and continuous.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá noting that mirror and lights have no physical connection yet the relationship of rays is firm and continuous; opens the section on images.

selected.text: In any case, whether it be difficult or easy, you are ever before my eyes and are not forgotten. I am always thinking of those loving friends
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá assuring that whether things are hard or easy the friends are ever before His eyes; constancy in all conditions.

selected.text: I swear by the Ancient Beauty, the sweetness of the company of true friends, like honey, makes the palate of heart and soul sugary and sweet.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá swearing that the company of true friends is sweet as honey to heart and soul; the sweetness of fellowship.

selected.text: Praise be to God that our companionship, love and fellowship remain firm, for our intimacy is at the Sacred Threshold of the All-Glorious Lord
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying their companionship remains firm because their intimacy is at the Sacred Threshold; the shared center of fellowship.

selected.text: Yes, surely sincere prayer always has its effect, and it has a great influence in the other word. We are never cut off from those who are there.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that sincere prayer has great influence in the other world and we are never cut off from those who are there; prayer for the departed.

selected.text: Come thou forth that I may hear thy melodies and thou mayest hear Mine
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh calling the reader to come forth that each may hear the other’s melodies; a reciprocal image of listening.

selected.text: After these meetings there is no separation, there is a union that knows no dispersion. The president of that gathering is His Holiness Baha'u'llah.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that after these meetings there is no separation, for Bahá’u’lláh presides over the gathering; the spiritual center of the assembly.

selected.text: friends of 'Abdu'l-Baha! Though I am in the clime of Joseph of Canaan, yet in spirit and heart I am the intimate companion and confidant of the spiritual
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that though in the clime of Joseph of Canaan He is the intimate companion of the spiritual friends; presence from afar.

selected.text: I send thee the answer spiritually so that the signs of the address may become manifest in thy heart. Verily thou art with me in spirit at all times.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá sending an answer spiritually so that its signs appear in the recipient’s heart; a spiritual reply.

selected.text: I trust that the ideal bonds of spiritual communication may ever become stronger and firmer between us. These celestial ties of communion are eternal.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to departing pilgrims that the celestial ties of communion are eternal and should grow stronger; continuity of the bond.

selected.text: Given this connection, there is no disconnection that would necessitate expression through speech. Souls and hearts are in conversation with each other
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that given this connection no expression through speech is needed, since souls and hearts converse; inward conversation.

selected.text: If there is outward delay in sending letters, there is no harm, for praise be to God, the inner doors are open and spiritual missives are in circulation.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh saying outward delay in letters does no harm because the inner doors are open and spiritual missives circulate; Bahá’u’lláh’s word on delayed replies.

selected.text: There is a spiritual understanding or communication. You are always associating or affiliating with Me. Although outwardly far away physically, but in spirit you are near
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that there is a spiritual understanding by which the hearers, though far physically, are near in spirit; a plain spoken statement.

selected.text: You will establish a connection between the divine realm and the material world, and become an intermediary between the realm of place and placelessness.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying the recipient will become an intermediary between the divine realm and the material world; the believer as a link between worlds.

selected.text: Though it was brief, the communication between hearts is detailed. The spiritual messenger and the conscientious courier are constantly coming and going
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that though a letter was brief, communication between hearts is detailed; a neat contrast of outer and inner.

selected.text: Physical distance has no effect - the far is near and the absent is present, for spiritual affinity exists between us and divine connection is established.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying the far is near and the absent present because spiritual affinity and divine connection exist; a compact formulation.

selected.text: Likewise, though I was remote in so far as the body is concerned, I was near to the friends in heart and spirit and close to the believers in that assembly.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that though remote in body He was near to the believers in that assembly; presence in a particular assembly.

selected.text: Although the physical tongue and earthly pen and ink may grow weary, yet the spiritual tongue and the conscious pen are ever engaged in speech and writing.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying the earthly pen may tire but the spiritual tongue and conscious pen are ever engaged; an image of inexhaustible inner writing.

selected.text: But praise be to God, that despite the fact that Baha'is do not know one another's language, they understand with their hearts and become infinitely happy
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that Bahá’ís who do not know one another’s language understand with their hearts and become happy; a practical example.

selected.text: Many were the nights and days we conversed with perfect joy and spirit, spoke of God's eternal bounty, and gave glad tidings of the appearance of the Kingdom
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling nights and days of joyful conversation about God’s bounty and the Kingdom; the fruit of fellowship in speech.

selected.text: Though a thousand leagues of mountain, plain and desert separate us, yet the fragrance of love perfumes our nostrils and fills our souls with its sweet scent.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that despite a thousand leagues of mountain and desert the fragrance of love fills their souls; fragrance across distance.

selected.text: You are ever my companion and confidant; despite the distance from Shiraz, you are before me and in my thoughts, though outwardly you are in Khata and Khutan
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá assuring a distant friend that they are ever His companion, before Him and in His thoughts; a brief portrait.

selected.text: Abdul-Baha was present in spirit and heart although absent in body. That meeting was exceedingly bright, and as the rose-garden, emitted a pleasant fragrance.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying He was present in spirit at a meeting that was bright and fragrant as a rose-garden; a particular gathering.

selected.text: Although I have not attained the honor of your presence physically, yet by virtue of "souls are like recruited troops" I have found the cord of love connected
selected.reason: Letter of the Báb finding the cord of love connected without meeting, by virtue of “souls are like recruited troops”; widens the voices of the guide.

selected.text: among the friends there is speech and utterance without lips or tongue, and without pen, ink and paper there is correspondence in the realm of heart and spirit
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on speech without lips or tongue and correspondence without pen and paper in the realm of heart and spirit; the language of the heart.

selected.text: when 'Abdu'l-Baha remembers the faces and city of those dear ones, his surroundings become like the land of Khutan and his gathering becomes fragrant with musk
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that remembering the faces of dear ones makes His gathering fragrant with musk; a vivid image of remembrance.

selected.text: Thou art present in spirit in a meeting (in Acca) in which the gifts of God are radiating, even though thou art remote in regard to body in the far away land.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá telling a distant believer that they are present in spirit in a meeting where the gifts of God radiate; presence in the gathering.

selected.text: It is as though the breathings of the Holy Spirit appear from the effect of your pen and the effulgences of the light of fellowship shine forth from its letters.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh saying the breathings of the Holy Spirit appear from a correspondent’s pen and the light of fellowship shines from its letters; praise of a particular writer.

selected.text: For this love emanates from connection with the love of the Ancient Beauty and is in truth a wave from the waves of the Most Great Sea in this greatest gathering
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying this love emanates from the love of the Ancient Beauty and is a wave from the Most Great Sea; traces love to its source.

selected.text: My spirit communicates with you. It annihilates space and time. There are some believers in Persia with whom my spirit always speaks but I have never seen them.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that His spirit annihilates space and time and speaks with believers in Persia He has never seen; striking personal testimony.

selected.text: in this gathering, especially since at the Divine Threshold you have a special representative like Ghulamrida Khan, who constantly has your mention on his tongue - indeed it forms the very words of his prayers. He remembers you often verbally and always continuously in his heart
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing Ghulamrida Khan, whose prayers are formed of the recipient’s mention; a person who carries remembrance for another.

selected.text: Though they are physically far, they are spiritually present in the gathering, and though they are outwardly separated, in heart they are in the inhabited House.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying the physically distant are spiritually present in the gathering and in heart within the inhabited House; presence in the gathering.

selected.text: Rest assured that I do not rest for a moment without remembering the friends, and my tongue adorns itself with nothing but praise of the servants of the Threshold.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá assuring that He does not rest without remembering the friends and praising the servants of the Threshold; remembrance joined to praise.

selected.text: in the spiritual world I shall seek heavenly outpourings for you at every moment. At dawn, turn to the Abha Kingdom and you will find 'Abdu'l-Baha as your companion.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promising to seek heavenly outpourings for the recipient and bidding them turn at dawn to the Abha Kingdom to find Him as companion; the closing invitation.

selected.text: your books of acceptance, sincerity, orientation, mention, praise, love and faithfulness are present before His face, and have attained both His sight and His hearing
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh describing a correspondent’s books of sincerity, love and faithfulness as present before His face and attaining His sight and hearing; letters reaching their goal.

selected.text: Although you are far and remote in that land, yet you are present and renowned at the Sacred Threshold. Nearness is through heart and soul, not through the weak body.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying nearness is through heart and soul, not through the weak body; a concise principle.

selected.text: Know, verily, I was with you in spirit during your assemblage in the meeting of the commemoration of God … and I perceived ye with my spirit on the Mount of Salvation
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá telling a gathering that He was with them in spirit during their commemoration of God; a particular gathering.

selected.text: By My life! The Most Exalted Pen hath been moved to make mention of thee in My mighty and impregnable Tablet, and through it tongues shall be opened in thy remembrance

selected.text: The secret whispers and melodies of heart and soul are attraction to and love of the Beloved, and the protected symbol and concealed mystery is the knowledge of the All-Merciful Lord. This is the firm and strong connection between us.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá naming attraction to the Beloved and knowledge of the All-Merciful as the firm connection between them; states the content of the bond.

selected.text: Although the physical eye is deprived, praise be to God that spiritual insight is privy to the mysteries of the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting. You are present in the divine court and exist and are witnessed in the heavenly gathering.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that though the physical eye is deprived, the recipient is witnessed in the heavenly gathering; the heavenly assembly.

selected.text: that a blessed soul from the inhabitants of America, while in the Holy Land, mentioned to Abdul-Baha the name of a man living in Asia, and with the utmost devotion requests the writing of a Tablet. … Praise be to God! What a communication
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá marvelling that an American believer in the Holy Land asked for a Tablet for a man living in Asia; shows the social reach of the spiritual bond.

selected.text: Though outwardly this letter is but traces upon paper, in reality it is the breathings of the spirit and the cause of victory. It imparts the intoxication of the heavenly wine and wafts the fragrance from the gardens of the Abha Kingdom.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying a letter outwardly traces on paper is in reality the breathings of the spirit and fragrance of the Abha Kingdom; contrasts outward and inward letter.

selected.text: Although outwardly pen and paper and leaf are the means of connection and expression of love and aspiration, yet in the eyes of those endowed with insight, this is that universal connection which has moved and continues to move the world.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh seeing in pen and paper, to those with insight, the universal connection that moves the world; enlarges the letter into a world-shaping bond.

selected.text: I hope from His boundless grace that He will make the spiritual bonds so firm and strong that there will be no need for pen and paper. The purpose is to be ever a companion and intimate friend, and always an associate and close companion.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping spiritual bonds grow so firm there is no need of pen and paper, the purpose being constant companionship; names what correspondence serves.

selected.text: Although thou wert not present in body at this Threshold, yet in spirit thou art, God willing, present at all times. They made mention of thee at this Court, engaged in remembrance of thee, and requested that mention be made on thy behalf.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that friends made mention of an absent recipient at the Threshold and asked for mention on their behalf; intercession by others.

selected.text: the blessed sacred leaf, your mother, constantly remembers you, has not a moment's rest, turns to the two blessed Holy Persons, seeks nearness to the Court, desires protection from the arrows of trials, and makes pilgrimage on your behalf
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing a mother who constantly remembers her child and makes pilgrimage on their behalf; a family portrait of remembrance.

selected.text: Know that you are present now in spirit, a confidant and intimate companion. I hope through God's bounty that wherever you are, whatever you do, whatever you think, whatever occupation you pursue, you will be here in spirit and conscience
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping that wherever the recipient goes and whatever they do they will be present in spirit; presence carried into daily life.

selected.text: Its Bestowals have established communication between the spirits. Its principles have ushered in a new era of spiritual brotherhood! Ere long ye shall observe that the splendours of the Kingdom of Abha have illumined the East and the West!
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the bestowals of the Cause have established communication between spirits and a new era of spiritual brotherhood; the collective horizon.

selected.text: but there was a clear messenger and faithful courier between us, and that reciprocal feeling of heart and conscience. Praise be to God that for this reason the spiritual connections are continuous and the conscientious feelings are sustained
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá naming the reciprocal feeling of heart and conscience a faithful courier between correspondents; an image of the inward messenger.

selected.text: The real meeting consists in the communication of heart. I hope that this communication will become strong, for the hearts which are spiritually related to each other, their meetings are eternal, both in this world and in the Universe of God.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying the real meeting is the communication of heart, whose meetings are eternal in this world and the Universe of God; defines real meeting.

selected.text: I swear by the Ancient Beauty that at all times we are gladdened by your mention and occupied with your remembrance. Forgetfulness finds no path to the heart and consciousness of those who long for you, and weakness and lassitude cannot enter.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá swearing that forgetfulness and lassitude cannot enter the hearts of those who long for the recipients; remembrance as oath.

selected.text: For day and night my call is "Ya Baha El Abha" and summoning the people to the Kingdom of Abha. The Knowing hearts comprehend these significances. The souls who turn their faces toward God will behold the lights of the Kingdom of Baha'u'llah.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that day and night He calls “Ya Baha El Abha” and summons people to the Kingdom; His own unceasing call.

selected.text: Therefore, those who circle the Kaaba of mystic knowledge and the lovers of the Beauty of the All-Merciful have a spiritual connection and a true and essential unity which results from the original unity and the realization of spiritual affection.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on lovers of the All-Merciful sharing a spiritual connection and essential unity born of original unity; names the source of affinity.

selected.text: Ye are the chanting birds, the mellifluous nightingales, and the divine parrots of Ind so sing ye all, without restrain and raise aloft your melodies. Perchance the ears of men may hearken thereunto and the hearts unravel the mysteries of your songs.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling the friends singing birds who should raise their melodies so hearts may unravel their mysteries; speech as song.

selected.text: The beloved of God must, like the roses of the rose-garden, send fragrant messages from one to another, receive strength from one another, and co-operate together, by the strength of the Kingdom. There is no greater means than communion and communication
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá urging the beloved of God, like roses, to send fragrant messages and co-operate, since there is no greater means than communion and communication; links fellowship to correspondence.

selected.text: I do greet thee from this Exalted Place, while thou art in that far distant country, and present to thee salutations and praise, and I see thee with the eye of the heart as though thou were present here and I speak to thee by the tongue of the Spirit
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá greeting a distant friend, seeing them with the eye of the heart and speaking by the tongue of the Spirit; an intimate image of presence.

selected.text: When this servant imagines that gathering, I find a new spirit and obtain great joy, and from afar I say: O gathering of friends! When you engage in remembrance of the All-Merciful in holy gatherings and intimate assemblies, remember this yearning one
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking a gathering, when engaged in remembrance of the All-Merciful, to remember this yearning one; how a gathering remembers the absent.

selected.text: The beloved of God are endowed with a particular language through which they express their feelings and converse with one another. The sun speaks to the existing beings, the cloud communicates with the earth and the gentle breeze whispers to the trees.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the beloved of God have a particular language, as the sun speaks to beings and the breeze whispers to the trees; natural imagery of communion.

selected.text: Whereas thou canst see that when an Easterner meets a Westerner this immediately resulteth in fellowship, two intimate brothers from the same parents avoid and detest each other. What does this indicate to? Is it not a proof for the unity of souls and spiritual
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting the fellowship of Easterner and Westerner with estranged brothers as a proof of the unity of souls; an argument from experience.

selected.text: spiritual letters are continually and uninterruptedly descending from the Supreme Concourse and the Kingdom of ABHA. That holy Messenger is eternal and perennial and His messages come to the heart successively and the verses of oneness are read therein.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying spiritual letters descend continually from the Supreme Concourse and verses of oneness are read in the heart; the heavenly source of communion.

selected.text: O longtime friend! For some time now you have forgotten your friend and remained silent in remembering him - no greetings, no message, no messenger, and no word - even though you know that you are always in my thoughts and are the companion in the gathering of my heart
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá gently reproaching a longtime friend for silence while affirming the friend is always in His thoughts; human warmth in a request for news.

selected.text: O thou who gazest upon the Abha Kingdom! Thus far numerous letters have been sent, and drops from the surging oceans of love that wave in the essence of the heart have been expressed. And now again we have thought of thee and set about penning this letter.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling numerous letters sent as drops from surging oceans of love and turning again to write; shows persistent correspondence.

selected.text: friends! selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting Adhirbayjan and Canaan and saying the spiritual bonds are firm and the light of divine oneness guides; grounds nearness in oneness.

selected.text: Though we may be hidden from outward sight, in the world of heart and soul we are visible and manifest. Though the body may be far removed, the spirit is ever intimate with the grace of meeting and presence, and hearts are close and connected to each other.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that though hidden from outward sight they are visible in the world of heart and soul; a balanced paradox.

selected.text: Though ye are in that region and we in this, yet we are neighbors and companions, intimates and dwellers in the same place, for we abide beneath the shade of the same Tree of Hope and dwell in the same Paradise of Delight. We are in one gathering and one home.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying the separated are neighbours beneath one Tree of Hope in one Paradise, in one gathering and one home; a shared spiritual center.

selected.text: They see all as it affects the spirit. A great joy, a great sorrow, a sin, or a good deed: as these things darken or cloud the soul, or cause it to rise into greater light, so they see every earth event that touches you for good or ill, reflected in your soul.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the departed see earthly events as they affect the soul, darkening it or raising it into light; describes their perception.

selected.text: Again I write and am gladdened and pleased to remember you. I grow neither weary nor tired, for the glad tidings of the Abha Kingdom give such strength that at every moment new life is gained and one becomes alive through remembrance and mention of the friends.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying He never wearies of writing, for remembrance of the friends brings new life at every moment; remembrance as renewal.

selected.text: The beloved of God although they are far away in body, in reality, in spirit, they are present. They exist here, though they are not present. If spiritual meeting were not possible I would go to meet all the believers in America, because I am anxious to meet them
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the beloved of God are present though far away, and that if spiritual meeting were impossible He would go to meet them all; a candid example.

selected.text: The answer is what is written on the tablet of your heart. That which is written upon paper is subject to corruption and various accidents, such as consumption by fire and moth, but that which is inscribed on the tablet of the heart is imperishable and everlasting.
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that writing on the tablet of the heart is imperishable while paper is subject to fire and moth; parallels Paul’s letter written in the heart.

selected.text: In truth, thou art present in this gathering, and night and day we are intimate companions. … Indeed, in the private chamber of the heart of the friends we are confidants of one another, and in the secret sanctuary of the soul we are intimate companions day and night
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that in the private chamber of the heart and the sanctuary of the soul the friends are confidants day and night; intimacy of the gathering.

selected.text: Thy letter was received. It was a proof to thy faith and assurance. The heart and the spirit of Abdul Baha is extremely tender. Therefore, continually he begs from the Kingdom of Abha inexhaustible favors for the friends of God and the maidservants of the Merciful.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying His heart is tender and so He continually begs favours from the Kingdom for the friends; remembrance as intercession.

selected.text: The electric current arrived bearing news of thy arrival. This news was a clear glad-tiding and a trustworthy herald. After being informed, we proceeded to the Holy Court where it was presented before the countenance of the Lord and was blessed to attain His hearing.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh telling how news arriving by electric current was presented before the Lord and attained His hearing; an instance of telegraphic news.

selected.text: Although I have been deprived and separated from seeing the faces of friends with my eyes, praise be to God I am a companion and confidant in heart and soul, and not a moment passes that you do not come to mind, not a breath goes by except that you cross my thoughts.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that though deprived of seeing the friends, not a breath passes without their crossing His thoughts; constant remembrance.

selected.text: and tell him: Though absent you are present, though hidden you are manifest - that is, you are beloved of the hearts of friends and mentioned in the gathering of companions. selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding a messenger tell someone that though absent they are present and mentioned at the Sacred Threshold; a message of presence.

selected.text: For the servants of the threshold of the Most Glorious Beauty have spiritual connections and established spiritual attachments. Even if outwardly they do not write or speak, inwardly they are captivated by love for one another and are companions and associates of each other.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying the servants of the threshold are inwardly bound by love even if outwardly they neither write nor speak; affinity beyond words.

selected.text: O fruit of the Tree of Mercy! A letter was sent several days ago, and now too this letter is being written through His Holiness the Martyr, son of the Martyr, so that you may know that you are always mentioned in this presence and are witnessed and renowned in this gathering.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá sending another letter so the recipient may know they are always mentioned in His presence; correspondence as assurance of remembrance.

selected.text: Due to the intensity of the connection between hearts, forms have taken on the properties of essences, metaphor has found the effect of reality, words have acquired the power of meanings, and expressions have become the truth of allusions and glad tidings of abstract meanings.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying the intensity of connection gives metaphor the effect of reality and words the power of meanings; reflects on the images themselves.

selected.text: Thou art in India and we are in Syria, and though hundreds, nay thousands, of leagues separate us, yet thou art present in our gathering, thou art a bird of this meadow, a nightingale of this rose garden. We are gladdened by thy remembrance and freed from sorrow by thy mention.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá telling a friend in India that across thousands of leagues they are a nightingale of His rose garden; a vivid portrait.

selected.text: This much sufficeth: that from the depths of my heart I love you. This love between me and you is eternal. Time and place shall not hinder it. Though I be in the East, my spirit and my heart are with you. I perceive the feelings of your conscience. Whenever
selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá declaring His love eternal and unhindered by time and place, perceiving the feelings of His hearers’ consciences; a personal assurance.

selected.text: Although thou art absent and out of sight yet in reality thou art here with us. Materially thou art far but spiritually thou art very close. Thou art deprived of the physical presence of this company but in reality thou art a confidant of the well-guarded mystery of the spirit.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling an absent friend, deprived of physical presence, a confidant of the well-guarded mystery of the spirit; reassurance to the absent.

selected.text: in this world hath no significance, and praise be to God, spiritual nearness in the world of the spirit is real and evident. Therefore, think not that thou art distant and estranged. Rather, thou art present in this gathering
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá telling a friend not to think themselves distant, for spiritual nearness is real and they are present in the gathering; reassurance.

selected.text: Although in body we are far from one another, yet--praise be to God!--with life and heart we are present in one assembly; we enjoy the spiritual meeting, abide under the shadow of one Blessed Tree, are attracted to the beauty of one Beloved and gaze in the direction of one Object.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá affirming that those far apart in body are present with life and heart in one assembly, gazing toward one Object; states the guide’s central paradox.

selected.text: How can oblivion find way here? To cease to think of thee is impossible - at every moment I behold thee and call thee to mind. How then can I forget thee? So enthralled and enlivened is that loving friend with the remembrance of the All-Merciful that he can never fade from memory
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking how oblivion could find its way, since He beholds the friend at every moment; a lively denial of forgetting.

selected.text: In this interminable journey, whenever the thought of the friends passed through my mind, I found myself transported from my travels to the familiar environment of home; an extraordinary feeling of happiness overcame me; and my pain and weariness were converted into ease and rest
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling how the thought of the friends during an interminable journey turned pain and weariness into ease and rest; opens the guide with presence through remembrance.

selected.text: Outwardly there has been no news and no message, no letter and no greeting; but the ideal relations have been strong and unshakable. From the rose-garden of the hearts of the friends we smelt sweet and perfuming fragrances. This was indeed conducive to the consolation of the souls.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that with no letter or greeting the ideal relations stayed strong and fragrances came from the friends’ hearts; consolation without news.

selected.text: During these days when they were the companion of these servants, during the time of visiting the circumambulation point of the Supreme Concourse, they would visit on behalf of you and all relations, and likewise would feast by proxy in the name of those leaves, and all was accepted.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing visits and a feast made by proxy for absent relations, all accepted; distinctive practical example.

selected.text: Observe how the bounties of Baha'u'llah have connected hearts such that while you are in that most distant region and 'Abdu'l-Baha is in this blessed spot, He is stirred in remembrance of you and is your intimate companion in heart and soul - we are in one gathering and one dwelling.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observing how the bounties of Bahá’u’lláh connect hearts so that a distant friend and He are in one gathering; grounds the bond religiously.

selected.text: O you who have purified your face for God, and have awakened and awakened every sleeper, and have become aware and made every heedless one aware, and have heard and made every possessor of ears hear and understand, and have seen and removed the veil from every possessor of lofty vision.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising one who, having awakened, awakened others and made the heedless aware; connection turned outward.

selected.text: Your letter was received and, despite lack of time, due to the intensity of love an immediate reply is being written, so that you may praise the favors of the Blessed Beauty Who has made 'Abdu'l-Baha so enamored with you that upon receiving your letter He proceeded at once to write a reply.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá replying at once despite lack of time because of the intensity of love; a practical sign of affection in correspondence.

selected.text: Our hearts like unto pure mirrors receive the impressions and these spiritual images are reflected from one mirror upon another without the medium of language. selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that pure-hearted hearers understand each other as images pass between mirrors without language; a narrative application.

selected.text: In the meeting the words of the Believers must be about God and the Wisdom of God, or to illustrate the proofs and signs of God. selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the words of believers in meetings must be for the enlightenment and enkindlement of others; carries the questions’ theme of kinder speech.

selected.text: Observe the bounty of God, that 'Abdu'l-Baha, in the Most Great Prison, facing the temple of the people of Christ, is occupied with thy remembrance … But I, O Khudabakhsh, speak with heart and soul, and by God I have love for thee and am occupied with thy remembrance. selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá addressing Khudabakhsh with love from the Most Great Prison and saying heartfelt remembrance produces an effect; a personal portrait.

selected.reason: Recorded words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that in prayer there is a mingling of condition and the departed may offer suggestions, sometimes in sleep, but no phenomenal intercourse; a necessary qualification.

selected.text: Though to outward seeming ye are far from here but in reality ye are present before me. selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying the power of the word of God has united scattered souls into one spirit, one soul, one body; a foundational statement on the Word.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá distinguishing correspondence by letters, shared by all, from heart-to-heart communion belonging to the people of light; frames the section on the pen.

selected.text: Though some time has passed since I wrote you letters with pen and ink, yet in the world of spirit and in my heart I am, at all times, in communion with the friends of the Abha Beauty. selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá assuring that, despite a gap in letters, in spirit He has not ceased corresponding with the friends for a single breath; unbroken communion behind written silence.

selected.text: Always one end of the wire is fixed in the hearts of the East and the other end fixed in the hearts of the West. selected.text: Though outwardly thou art far from sight and view and removed from this gathering, yet I swear by the light shining from the Supreme Horizon that in truth all the branches of the Blessed Tree are at all times present in this gathering of the All-Merciful and are manifest and visible in this spiritual assembly.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá swearing that all the branches of the Blessed Tree are present in the gathering of the All-Merciful though outwardly far; the spiritual assembly.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá confirming that spiritual communications continued when correspondence was cut off, for every heart is a mirror of hearts; joins two themes.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá linking the Holy Land and America through divine oneness and hoping for companionship in the Kingdom; carries the bond toward the next world.

selected.text: God, exalted be His glory, hath made the pen a translator in such wise that it may express and convey the love that dwelleth in the hearts and souls of the friends. selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh describing the pen as a translator of the love dwelling in hearts, upon which the connection of the world depends; the foundational text on the pen’s role.

selected.text: I hope that the friends of God will not need outward correspondence, but rather will inhale spiritual breezes from the direction of grace and acquire and receive unlimited bounties from the invisible Kingdom. selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping the friends will not need outward correspondence but receive spiritual letters from the Supreme Concourse; points beyond human letters.

selected.text: Whatever I write, the protected secret of the heart is not revealed and the truth of the meanings does not become known, for both pen and ink are strangers.
